note: Test vectors for the derivative store contract (ADR 0123), byte-exact and language-neutral: Python and TypeScript must both reproduce every one. Computed from the definition with Python struct, hashlib and NumPy, and again with Bun node:crypto, all equal; computed, not measured on any NEMAR data. Never change a vector to make code pass: the maintainer decides whether the vector or the code is wrong. The key fields are full-string matches, so a Python consumer must use re.fullmatch (its $ also matches before a trailing line feed). In `refused`, the JSON string NaN stands for a NaN number, which JSON cannot hold.
note_locations: Vectors store_locations and input_digest_v2 (ADR 0123, amendment 2026-11-16), added to the version 1 vectors above, which are unchanged. Computed from the definition with Python json, struct, hashlib and math, and again with Bun, all equal; computed, not measured on any NEMAR data. Read this file with JSON.parse or json.loads, never through an object literal: __proto__ is an own key in the vector named inherited names, and the integer in the vector named an integer too large for binary64 has 400 digits (JSON.parse reads it as Infinity, Python as an int). In each vector the text is exactly what is hashed (the digest of an input digest vector is sha256: and the SHA-256 of its text), and a vector with also_equal_to has the digest of the vector it names. A vector with also_with lists variants that a reader applies as a shallow merge over the case (a variant's labels or attributes replace the case's) and that give the same text. In refused, the field of an input_digest_v2 entry is the DerivativeContractError field.

input_digest.name: code point order
input_digest.note: U+FF61 sorts before U+1F600 by code point (UTF-8 bytes); UTF-16 units put U+1F600 first. The rows may arrive in either order; they are stored with U+1F600 first, so one pass catches both a missing sort and a UTF-16 sort.
